short.hook: A 2,900-year-old mountain sanctuary on Euboea was found without a temple.
script: A 2,900-year-old mountain sanctuary on Euboea was found without a temple.
Excavations revealed pottery from the ninth century BC and burned sheep bones.
These suggest ritual sacrifices and offerings made by residents of Eretria.
An inscription mentioning 'Artemis Olympia' hints at a possible cult of Artemis.
Yet no altar or building was ever discovered at the summit site.
Could the sanctuary have been a spiritual place without physical structures?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A 2,900-year-old mountain sanctuary on Euboea’s Mount Olympos was uncovered during 2025–2026 surveys. Pottery from the ninth century BC and burned animal bones suggest ritual sacrifices. An inscription from Eretria mentioning 'Artemis Olympia' may indicate worship of the goddess. However, no temple or altar was found. Researchers note mountain sanctuaries were common, though often lacking physical remains. Source: UA.News, https://ua.news/en/dovkolo-svitu/na-gretskii-evbeyi-znaishli-2900-richne-girske-sviatilishche-live-science
